notes: Authored corpus for the real_microplastics quality case: two peer-review-style documents and two web documents that disagree about what detection implies. Names, venues and DOIs are fictional; the documents are written for this evaluation. Replace docs/*.md to evaluate real sources.

sources.title: Urinary Microplastic Concentrations and Inflammatory Markers in a Prospective Cohort
sources.snippet: A cohort of 1,240 adults found a small association between urinary particle concentration and C-reactive protein.
sources.abstract: We measured microplastic particle concentrations in repeated urine samples from 1,240 adults and tested associations with three inflammatory markers. Higher concentrations were associated with elevated C-reactive protein, with a 0.12 milligram per litre increase per interquartile range. The design cannot establish causality.

sources.title: A Systematic Review of Microplastic Toxicology: What the Animal and Human Evidence Supports
sources.snippet: Of 40 experimental studies, none demonstrated a consistent adverse effect at concentrations reported in drinking water.
sources.abstract: We reviewed 40 experimental studies of microplastic exposure, of which 31 were rodent studies and 9 were human biomarker studies. No study demonstrated a consistent adverse effect at concentrations reported in drinking water, and the human evidence does not show a dose-response relationship.

sources.title: Consumer Testing Report: Microplastics in Municipal Drinking Water
sources.snippet: Ninety percent of 259 tap water samples contained at least one plastic particle; the maximum was 61 particles per litre.

sources.title: Risk Assessment of Microplastics in Drinking Water: Current Position
sources.snippet: No epidemiological study has reported a health outcome associated with drinking-water microplastic exposure; the margin to the lowest effect dose is about a thousandfold.
